title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
claim: Distilled students systematically mismatch the teacher's spectrum, underfitting on sparse graphs and overfitting on dense ones, and our method narrows both gaps.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: stacked spectra, direction sketches, bar chart with shaded regime bands
description: Three-panel figure. Panel (a) has two stacked bar charts of singular values against singular index. The top chart, titled Mode 1 spectral underfit for sparse graphs, shows the teacher spectrum (blue) decaying slowly, GLNN (red) decaying fast, and G²MLP (green) in between. The bottom chart, titled Mode 2 spectral overfit for dense graphs, shows the teacher collapsing quickly, GLNN (red) staying high, and G²MLP (green) collapsing faster. Orange curved arrows carry annotations such as 'Our spectrum extends further'. Each legend gives an effective rank. Panel (b) shows small 2-D vector sketches. Blue teacher arrows and red student arrows are drawn together with grey dashed arrows for missing directions, or red dashed arrows for extra noise directions. Panel (c) is a grouped bar chart of signed rank gap for five datasets, with red GLNN bars and green G²MLP bars and error bars. Orange and blue background bands mark the two modes. The eye goes first to the colored bars and the tall red +7.6 bar.
caption: Two spectral failure modes of GNN-to-MLP distillation. (a) Singular-value spectra: GLNN exhibits spectral underfit on sparse graphs and spectral overfit on dense graphs. (b) Rank-direction sketch. (c) Per-dataset rank gap; bands mark the dominant mismatch channel (Table [ref]).
abstract: GNN-to-MLP distillation aims to retain the predictive accuracy of a message-passing teacher while deploying a graph-free MLP at inference. Existing methods mainly transfer node-wise predictions or use confidence-based reweighting, but they do not specify where the student should preserve the teacher's graph-induced geometry. We show that this omission leads to two spectral failure modes in the student's representation space. On sparse graphs, the student suffers from spectral underfit, missing high-energy teacher directions induced by aggregation. On dense graphs, it suffers from spectral overfit, retaining spurious directions that the teacher has collapsed through aggregation. Motivated by an energy-weighted teacher-student alignment objective, we propose Graph Geometry-aware MLP (G^2MLP), a training-time distillation framework guided by Ollivier-Ricci curvature. Curvature acts as a local proxy for allocating supervision between prediction-level and representation-level alignment. The deployed model is a standard MLP with no graph access at inference. Across node-classification benchmarks, G^2MLP improves over graph-free distillation baselines in most settings, reduces the teacher-student rank gap in both regimes, and transfers to Graph Transformer teachers and link prediction.
